what_happened: The job to refuse readings that omit a bullet from the request's acceptance list was rejected at the final verdict. One of 8 acceptance criteria was unmet: the criterion that the change refuses more readings and that the higher refusal rate is intended (expected about 10% newly refused, an estimate). There were two major findings and no blockers. First, behavior criterion 6 was unmet because its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). Second, the coverage rule in crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs (specific_stems, uncovered_bullets) discards the bullet words that the request's prose repeats and judges coverage on the incidental words left over. So it wrongly refuses readings that cover every bullet, and it catches the motivating case only by an accident of word forms. No checks are listed as failed.
cause: A new refusal rule was built and tuned from the wording of the reading and invented fixtures, not by running it over the recorded requests and readings it is meant to judge. Nothing in the producer's flow required a replay of real past readings before the final verdict. The word-matching heuristic (stripping words shared with the prose) therefore passed its own tests but gave false refusals on real shapes. The behavior-criterion evidence rule (D43) was also not surfaced to the producer, so command evidence was missing. Both gaps were found only by the verifier.
prevention: Add a code check that runs any new reading-refusal or matching rule over the recorded past requests and accepted readings, with the old and new builds, before the producer finishes. It reports newly refused readings that cover all bullets as false refusals. Test fixtures for the rule must be taken from recorded requests. The producer's report must list the commands run with their output as evidence for behavior criteria.
proposed_request: Fix the reading coverage rule in crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs so it refuses a reading only when it omits a request acceptance bullet. Outcome: a reading that covers every bullet of a real past request is never refused, and a reading that drops a bullet is refused. The rule must not discard words just because the request's prose repeats them; judge each bullet by its own content words. Acceptance: (1) a test replays the rule over recorded past requests and their accepted readings and shows zero false refusals on readings that cover every bullet; (2) fixtures are taken from recorded request shapes, including the motivating case, not invented; (3) the new refusal rate over those recorded requests is measured and stated, and the criterion that declares the higher refusal rate intended cites that measured figure; (4) the behavior criteria cite the commands that ran and their output; (5) cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test pass; (6) CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
